chunks.label: Bath and toilet
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask for the toilet and talk about bathing.
chunks.interference: Ofuro takes hairu but shawaa takes abiru.

chunks.label: Clothes and shoes
chunks.rationale: Lets you name what you wear and take your shoes off.
chunks.interference: Fuku goes on with kiru, but shoes, socks and trousers with haku.

chunks.label: Before you go out
chunks.rationale: Lets you check you've got everything before leaving.
chunks.interference: Kagi means both key and lock.

chunks.label: Phone and gadgets
chunks.rationale: Lets you swap numbers and talk about your phone, watch and camera.
chunks.interference: Tokei is both a clock and a watch.

chunks.label: Living room things
chunks.rationale: Lets you turn the TV and lights on and off and find a seat.
chunks.interference: Denki in a room means the light, not electricity.

chunks.label: Kitchen and table
chunks.rationale: Lets you set the table and find things in the fridge.
chunks.interference: Reizouko (fridge) and reitouko (freezer) differ by one sound.

chunks.label: Bed and sleep
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about going to bed and where people sleep.

chunks.label: Doors and windows
chunks.rationale: Lets you open up, shut up and say where something was left.
chunks.interference: Genkan is a home's entrance; a building's is iriguchi.

chunks.label: Eating and drinking out
chunks.rationale: Lets you suggest a place to eat, drink or take a break.
chunks.interference: Resutoran means a sit-down, usually Western place, not any eatery.

chunks.label: Errands in town
chunks.rationale: Lets you say where you're popping out to.
chunks.interference: Biyouin (hair salon) sounds close to byouin (hospital).

chunks.label: Meeting points
chunks.rationale: Lets you arrange where to meet.
chunks.interference: Iriguchi (entrance) is easy to swap with deguchi (exit).

chunks.label: Bags and boxes
chunks.rationale: Lets you name what you carry things in and turn down a shop bag.
chunks.interference: Three bag words: kaban is general, baggu a fashion bag, fukuro a soft carrier bag.

chunks.label: Gifts and letters
chunks.rationale: Lets you give a present, return the favour and write to someone.
chunks.interference: Okaeshi is also what shop staff say when handing over change.

chunks.label: Doing the laundry
chunks.rationale: Lets you do the washing and hang it out.
chunks.interference: Sentaku (the chore), sentakumono (the clothes) and sentakuki (the machine) sound alike.

chunks.label: Cleaning and chores
chunks.rationale: Lets you share the cleaning and take the rubbish out.
chunks.interference: Souji is cleaning a room; washing clothes is sentaku.

chunks.label: Where you live
chunks.rationale: Lets you say where you live and where you're from.
chunks.interference: Katei is the household, not the building (ie or uchi).

chunks.label: Buildings and institutions
chunks.rationale: Lets you point out buildings, the stairs inside, and places like kindergartens and care homes.
chunks.interference: Biru is a building, never a bill to pay.
